title: Finite binder expansion
summary: Approved 24-slice binder tranche with a mandatory human checkpoint after the reversible finite-sum exemplar.

sourceRefs.summary: Run-contract target that explains why this generated contract exists.
User-approved 24-slice plan, preservation boundary, visual checkpoint, promotion criteria, and exact stop conditions.
Canonical sum exemplar, product pressure, and binder sharing boundary.

allowedWork: Narrow the planned capability to finite binder expansion without claiming calculus coverage.
Add typed finite sum and product roles, range and scope legality, expansion lineage, diagnostics, case coverage, and corpora.
Build one reversible Native KaTeX finite-sum exemplar and stop for human visual review before product pressure.
After explicit visual approval, add one finite-product pressure caller and promote only caller-proven shared infrastructure.
Add governed discovery, authoring, readiness, exact browser evidence, and bundle evidence for the narrow family.
disallowedWork: No infinite sums, sequences, recurrence evaluation, integrals, differentiation, Taylor series, arbitrary substitution, or arithmetic evaluation.
No universal binder AST, generic calculus family, inferred semantic truth, or generic visual fallback.
No changes to existing choreography, public lessons, reader layouts, graph families, code frontends, or live-model behavior.
No product presentation generalization before explicit approval of the finite-sum visual checkpoint.
goal: Establish one human-approved finite-sum expansion, pressure its binder semantics with a finite product, and promote only proved scope, iteration, lineage, authoring, and evidence seams.
commitCadence: One independently reversible commit per completed slice.
stopConditions: Stop on ambiguous scope truth, accidental capture, false identity persistence, or unsupported semantic inference.
Stop on duplicate paint, terminal snapping, a second clock, CSS-owned animation, or any required change to existing approved choreography.
Stop after bf16 for explicit human visual approval before bf17 through bf24.
Stop if narrow Direct readiness cannot be derived from exact evidence or if bundle, architecture, lifecycle, or accessibility gates fail.
